content.text: {"results":[{"ref":"s0:54daf44d","offset":0,"totalChars":101666,"nextOffset":3152,"text":"{\"role\":\"toolResult\",\"toolCallId\":\"call_bUTcNRqFpFKyDUltTmTL2UKS|fc_096c958811ed9e6e016ab85c31d7e087d0821feb33fec559b4\",\"toolName\":\"bash\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"1374 [assistant] Yes — pi-omp's phased todo is the missing in-context layer, and it's already 80% of what Aaron gets from his scheduler thread: one `in_progress` at a time, auto-promote to the next open task, a sticky widget above the editor, reminders on `agent_end` when work is unfinished, and session persistence via `appendEntry`. What it lacks is exactly the two things you named: **hierarchy** (where am I in the tree) and **ownership** (what is doing which part). Here's how the pieces compose. ## Three layers, one hierarchy | Layer | Owns | Today | |---|---|---| | `todos/` files | the durable tree — items and the map (parent) across sessions | items only; no map shape yet | | **pi-omp `todo` widget** | the in-context slice — current map's children as phases, steps as tasks, one `in_progress` = *where you are*, owner = *who's on it* | phases/tasks/one in-progress; no owner, no nesting, no link to `todos/` | | pi-crumbs | provenance — uncommitted file ops = footprint of the side quest you're in | records `file_op`; no notion of fork | | pi-delegate | executes forks at root — scout/worker/reviewer with run ids | works; nothing shows which task a run is serving | ## The changes, smallest first 1. **`owner` and `ref` on a task** (`src/todo.ts` `TodoItem`, `todo` tool params, widget render). `owner` is `me`, a pi-delegate run label, or a Hop Op id; `ref` is the `todos/` id. The widget then answers \\\"what is doing what\\\" at a glance, and the existing rule \\\"todo calls never travel alone\\\" extends naturally: a `delegate` launch travels with `todo start <task> owner:<run>`. 2. **`fork` / `return` ops** for the stack. `fork <content>` pushes a phase named `↳ <content>` and marks the parent task in-progress with owner `fork`; `return` completes it and auto-promotes back to the parent — the existing promote logic already does the climb. One level of nesting shown in the widget is enough to answer \\\"where am I\\\"; deeper than that is the signal to delegate instead of descend. 3. **Point the round-trip at the map, not `TODO.md`.** `todo.file: \\\"TODO.md\\\"` writes a root backlog file, which is now a parallel backlog under our own rule. Change the import/export target to the active map todo in `todos\\n1382 [user] TOo complicated. And I need that thread map durable. What is Aaron's full suite of tools? This is first I've heard of a scheduler thread\\n1412 [assistant] Here's the full inventory, straight from the study's shopping list, and then the simplest durable-map answer. ## Aaron's full suite **Platform — Amp (the load-bearing piece).** Orbs (disposable cloud checkouts; 253 threads ran in them) · agent modes (low/medium/high/ultra ± fast) · Oracle (stronger-model diff review, 209 uses) · cross-thread reads (paste a thread URL, the agent reads it — his stated lock-in reason) · thread spawning plus `send_thread_message`/`thread_interact` (coordinator→worker wire) · schedules (cron-shaped threads, barely used) · project secrets inherited by "},{"ref":"s0:ea75652e:b2","offset":0,"totalChars":848,"nextOffset":null,"text":"{\"type\":\"toolCall\",\"id\":\"call_bUTcNRqFpFKyDUltTmTL2UKS|fc_096c958811ed9e6e016ab85c31d7e087d0821feb33fec559b4\",\"name\":\"bash\",\"arguments\":{\"command\":\"python3 - <<'PY'\\nimport json\\np='/Users/ssweens/.claude/projects/-Users-ssweens-src-pi-packages/9ef739b2-a82f-4d9c-ad69-0d1013ad5066.jsonl'\\nterms=('Aaron','Linear','Fixer','Lander','organized','side quest','thread map','thread ledger','tether')\\nwith open(p) as f:\\n  for i,line in enumerate(f,1):\\n    try:r=json.loads(line)\\n    except:continue\\n    m=r.get('message',{})\\n    c=m.get('content','')\\n    if isinstance(c,list): c=' '.join(x.get('text','') for x in c if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('type')=='text')\\n    text=' '.join(str(c).split())\\n    if any(t.lower() in text.lower() for t in terms) and len(text)>80:\\n      print(f'{i} [{m.get(\\\"role\\\")}] {text[:2200]}')\\nPY\",\"timeout\":30}}"}],"evidencePagesRemaining":1,"metadataSearchesRemaining":1}

The canonical repository is badlogic/pi-mono.\\\\n\\\\n## Testing Approach\\\\n\\\\nThe project uses **Node.js built-in `node:test` framework** (stable since Node 20) for all testing, avoiding external dependencies like Jest or Mocha. Test files live in `tests/`, `tests/integration/`, and `tests/e2e/` directories with `.test.ts` or `.test.mjs` suffix. Tests run via `node --test \\\\\\\"tests/**/*.test.ts\\\\\\\"` — Node 22.18+ supports native TypeScript, eliminating the need for tsx.\\\\n\\\\n**Run commands:**\\\\n```bash\\\\nnpm run test                # unit + integration\\\\nnpm run test:integration    # integration only\\\\nnpm run test:e2e           # end-to-end (requires PI_PLUGINS_E2E_REF env var)\\\\nnpm run test:coverage      # generates lcov reports\\\\nnode --test \\\\\\\"tests/**/*.test.ts\\\\\\\"  # direct invocation (or with tsx on Node <22.18)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nRecent commits demonstrate the testing philosophy: comprehensive verification that **tests actual behavior, not pre-existing state**. Commit 7e270a7 (September 22, 2026) fixed terminal tests that \\\\\\\"had been passing on pre-existing screen state without asserting on the actual startup state.\\\\\\\" The new tests verify the complete terminal experience from startup through multiline input.\\\\n\\\\nPackage-local `npm run check` runs strict TypeScript plus `node:test` through `tsx`, eliminating machine-specific dependencies.
